problem: A quadratic equation in the variable $x$ with real coefficients has a root $x=-1+\text{i}.$ Given that the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in the equation is $1,$ find the equation.

feedback.problem: A quadratic equation in the variable $x$ with real coefficients has a root $x=-3-2\text{i}.$ Given that the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in the equation is $5$, find the equation.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the quadratic equation has real coefficients and $x=-3-2\text{i}$ is a root, its conjugate $x=-3+2\text{i}$ must also be a root. Therefore, using the zero product property, we can write a quadratic equation with the required roots as follows:

$$
(x-(-3-2\text{i}))(x-(-3+2\text{i}))=0
$$

By expanding the parentheses, we can write the equation in standard form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-x(-3+2\text{i})-x(-3-2\text{i})+(-3-2\text{i})(-3+2\text{i}) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+3x-2x\text{i}+3x+2x\text{i}+9-4{\text{i}}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+6x+9+4 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+6x+13 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

This equation has roots $x=-3\pm 2\text{i},$ but the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ is not $5.$ Therefore, to find the desired equation, we multiply the equation above by $5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5({x}^{2}+6x+13) & =0 \\ 5{x}^{2}+30x+65 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
